chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Abu Imran, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He (peace be upon him) looked at a sandal with its strap tied, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) took it, untied it, and then said: 'Do not tie (it).'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on tying the straps of sandals according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) demonstrates the preferred method of securing footwear by untying a knotted strap, thereby establishing a normative practice (*sunnah*) for Muslims. This action reflects the broader Shia emphasis on adhering to the Prophet’s and Imams’ practical habits in daily life, distinguishing between obligatory rulings and recommended etiquette (*adab*). The ruling underscores the importance of simplicity and ease in personal adornment, aligning with the general Islamic principle of avoiding unnecessary complexity in permissible matters.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Ali Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Abu Islamil Al Sarraj, from Abu Imran, from a man,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having looked at a sandal with its straps tied, so Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> took hold of it and loosened it, then said: ‘Do not tie’.
en.sarwar: 12. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from abu ’Isma‘il al-Sarraj from ‘Imran from a man who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once looked at a shoe which had laces that were tied down. He (the Imam) picked it up, opened its laces and said, ‘This must not be tied down.’”
